content_units: Final-Exam Study Data Snapshot

Your 6-week data shows a clear pattern:   more total study time plus more practice tests generally matched higher quiz scores  , with the strongest stretch in   Weeks 3–5  . The standout peak is   Week 5   with   16 total study hours, 3 practice tests, and an average quiz score of 84  .
Recommended Charts and What They Reveal
Chart   What to Plot   What it would show   Key takeaway

Line chart: quiz score vs. week   Week on x-axis; avg quiz score on y-axis   Score trend over time from   72 → 84  , then a small dip to   80   in Week 6   Overall progress is strong, but the final week suggests consistency matters before exams

Stacked bar chart: subject study hours by week   Week on x-axis; math, history, science hours stacked   How weekly effort was distributed across subjects and how total study load changed   Total hours rose most in the highest-scoring weeks, especially Weeks 4–5

Scatter chart: practice tests vs. quiz score   practice tests on x-axis; avg quiz score on y-axis   Relationship between test practice and performance   More practice tests aligned with better scores, especially from Weeks 3–5
Most Important Trends Before Final Exams
-   Scores improved steadily from Week 1 to Week 5  : 72, 74, 78, 81, 84.
-   Week 5 was the strongest week  :
- Math: 8 hours
- History: 2 hours
- Science: 6 hours
- Practice tests: 3
- Avg quiz score:   84
-   Week 6 dipped slightly to 80   even though total hours stayed fairly high.
- This suggests that   how time is allocated   may matter as much as total time.
-   Practice testing appears especially valuable  :
- 1 practice test in Weeks 1–2 matched lower scores (72–74)
- 2–3 practice tests in Weeks 3–5 matched higher scores (78–84)
-   Science and math appear to be the strongest score-linked subjects  :
- Higher-scoring weeks generally had stronger math/science investment
- History hours increased sharply in Week 6, but the score did not keep rising
Exam-Focused Student Insights
- Prioritize   consistent math and science review  , since your best-performing weeks had strong hours in both.
- Keep doing   at least 2–3 practice tests per week  ; that is the clearest high-impact behavior in the data.
- Avoid shifting too much time into one subject at the expense of your strongest score drivers.
- For finals, your best template looks closest to   Week 5  : high total study time, balanced STEM focus, and maximum test practice.
